She has also sought access to documents and information concerning the family assets that were allegedly withheld from her despite repeated requests. The suit marks an escalation in the dispute between Venu Srinivasan and his daughter over the division of family wealth. The dispute centres on an arrangement reached between Venu Srinivasan, his wife Mallika Srinivasan and their children Lakshmi Venu and Sudarshan Venu in 2024. While Venu Srinivasan has maintained that a fair division was effected between his children, Lakshmi and Mallika Srinivasan have contested this position. Their contention is that the allocation of management responsibilities in the family businesses did not amount to a settlement of their respective economic interests in the family assets. items.title: Small mercies and large silences: The Supreme Court and the Constitution at 77
items.summary: Every November 26, the Supreme Court’s lawns are scrubbed, the ceremonial speeches are dusted off and the Republic congratulates itself on the durability of its founding charter. Constitution Day invites easy theatrics. Critics declare the document dead on arrival; loyalists hail the bench as an infallible shield against executive excess. The Supreme Court’s record across 2026 resists both caricatures. Over the past 11 months, the Court has displayed a striking split personality. When confronting the daily, retail indignities inflicted on ordinary citizens by municipal apathy, police high-handedness or bureaucratic drift, the Court has been remarkably imaginative. Yet, when asked to scrutinise the institutional architecture of democracy itself, the same Court has repeatedly blinked, deferred or stalled in the vestibule. The guardian of the sidewalk Take the Court’s record on individual dignity and personal liberty this year and there is genuine constitutional craftsmanship to admire.
